title: Kähler differentials of a polynomial algebra over an algebra
statement: Let $R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $e\ge0$ and $B=A[z_1,\dots,z_e]$ the polynomial ring, an $R$-algebra via $R\to A\to B$. Then the $B$-linear map $(B\otimes_A\Omega_{A/R})\oplus B^{e}\to\Omega_{B/R}$, $(b\otimes\mathrm d\alpha,(b_1,\dots,b_e))\mapsto b\,\mathrm d\alpha+\sum_jb_j\,\mathrm dz_j$ ($\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), is an isomorphism. In particular, if $\Omega_{A/R}$ is a free $A$-module of rank $d$, then $\Omega_{B/R}$ is a free $B$-module of rank $d+e$.

proof.text: Put B = MvPolynomial (Fin e) A and u = KaehlerDifferential.mapBaseChange R A B, v = KaehlerDifferential.map R A B B. Polynomial formal smoothness gives Subsingleton (Algebra.H1Cotangent A B). As in the Mathlib match of lem-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-differentials-injective, Algebra.H1Cotangent.exact_δ_mapBaseChange and LinearMap.injective_iff_eq_zero_of_exact imply injectivity of u, since the connecting map has zero domain.

By KaehlerDifferential.exact_mapBaseChange_map, ker v = range u and v(u x) = 0. Set q = (KaehlerDifferential.mvPolynomialBasis A (Fin e)).equivFun and s(b) = sum_j b_j d_R X_j. The formula map_D and the polynomial basis give v(s(b)) = q.symm b.

Construct the linear map f(x,b) = u(x) + s(b). If f(x,b) = f(y,c), applying v gives q.symm b = q.symm c, hence b = c; cancelling s(b) and using injectivity of u gives x = y. For omega, set b = q(v omega). Then v(omega - s(b)) = 0, so exactness yields x with u(x) = omega - s(b), proving f(x,b) = omega. LinearEquiv.ofBijective f gives precisely the displayed formula, by reflexivity.

For a basis beta indexed by Fin d, Module.Basis.baseChange yields a B-basis of B tensor_A Omega_A/R. Module.Basis.prod with Pi.basisFun gives a basis of the source of f indexed by Fin d + Fin e. Map this basis through f and reindex using finSumFinEquiv to obtain the required Fin (d+e) basis.
